standing_rules.description: optional: rules the profile carries for every seat of this CLI, over the team file's; they ride with the file's rules in every delivery

herdr_status.description: optional: whether herdr reports this CLI's agent status faithfully; with unreliable, a screen the profile reads idle counts as free whatever herdr says

exit.description: what is typed into an idle prompt to make the CLI exit; a profile carries this or exit_keys, never both

exit_keys.description: the keys that exit the CLI from its idle screen, in order, for a CLI that takes no exit text; a profile carries this or exit, never both

exit_clear.description: optional: the one key that empties the CLI's input box, sent only to clear an exit text that did not read back as typed; absent, the text is left for the owner

exit_confirm.description: optional: the one key that confirms the CLI's own exit question, sent by a stop on a screen the profile reads as an exit question; absent, a seat that asks the question cannot be stopped by asking

input.description: optional: the measured way into this CLI's input box — its clear keys and paste surface; absent, a delivery that finds unsent text holds it untouched, and a restart refuses

clear.description: the keys that empty the box on an idle screen, sent in order and repeated until the box reads empty

clear_working.description: the keys that empty the box during a running turn, measured on a CLI that takes text there

paste.description: how text is put back into the box: bracketed paste

mid_turn.description: whether this CLI takes text into its box while a turn runs; true requires clear_working, and false leaves a draft found on a working screen held

lobby_files.description: optional: the exact relative paths of regular files a capture showed this CLI writing in its working folder; absent, this CLI is not recorded as writing a file there

startup_reads.description: optional: paths this CLI reads at start in its working folder; a trailing slash names a directory and every file under it, and the lobby gate refuses each of these at any depth

not_started.description: optional: startup screens drawn before the CLI started a session; team down closes such a pane without typing, never choosing an option

mcp_inbox.description: optional: the team inbox's measured registration for this CLI; absent, its seats stay on the drop and typed legs

launch_args.description: arguments appended to the launch line; {seat}, {session}, {command} and {entry} are filled from the launch; {command_json}, {entry_json} and {seat_json} are the same values escaped for a double-quoted string inside a structured word; {file_args} is the server's --file pair as array elements when the launch named the team file, nothing otherwise

add.description: the CLI's own project-scope mcp add subcommand arguments, run in the seat's folder at launch; {seat}, {session}, {command} and {entry} are filled from the launch, and a whole {file} word is the launch's --file pair when it names the team file, nothing otherwise

target.description: the file add writes, relative to the seat's folder

file.description: a config file team writes itself, relative to the seat's folder

status_model.description: optional: absent, the CLI's screen doesn't show its model

last_used_model.description: optional: the CLI starts on its last-used model when a launch names none

unread_model.description: optional: launch names no model read from the screen but the launch line's own, labelled (from launch)

capture.description: The registered capture this record's predicate, label and extractor were taken from: the manifest's whole path, not a basename.

lobby_evidence.description: Codex only: a registered capture of the folder-only layout taken in the real lobby. Other CLIs must not claim it.

join.description: Join the rows after the anchor only when they prove one wrapped path: the first fills the wrap column, each later row starts at the indent. Off, the extractor refuses a run with more than one row.

indent.description: With join: the continuation column the capture draws.

wrap.description: With join: the column the capture's first wrapped row fills exactly.

turn_end.description: optional: the row that ends a turn — the CLI's own completion line. A `live` rule's region is the newest turn above the composer, and a turn-end row closes the turn it ends: every transcript row above the last one is a turn the pane has already scrolled past, so an error a completion ended is history while an error after the completion is still current. The pattern must match the whole row: "^…$". Absent: the whole paragraph above the composer is the newest turn.

ignore_case.description: Ignore ASCII case only: each letter matches its other case; no other character folds (a long s or a Kelvin sign reads as itself). The flag reaches every rule of the stage, the exceptions written beside a match included.

vendorNotice.description: A vendor's own notice — an update screen, for one. Never answered, and never a reading without a record: the `tested` range is the version the capture was taken on, and the loader requires it. The list form is refused.

ignore_case.description: Ignore ASCII case only: each letter matches its other case; no other character folds. The flag reaches every rule of the stage, the exceptions written beside a match included.

live.description: an any/all rule read on the live region alone: the composer's own rows and the newest turn above them, never a turn the window has scrolled past

at_composer.description: an any/all rule read on the block of rows directly above the composer alone: blanks are skipped, every non-blank row of the block must match the rule, and the block ends at the first row that does not (or at the profile's turn_end). A composer that cannot be read leaves the whole window to the rule, so a wall already held stays held

ignore_case.description: Ignore ASCII case only: each letter matches its other case; no other character folds (a long s or a Kelvin sign reads as itself). The flag is the entry's, so it reaches the except list beside the match.
Ignore ASCII case only: each letter matches its other case; no other character folds (a long s or a Kelvin sign reads as itself).

flag.description: The model id to suggest for this model and version. "{version}" is the seat's version.

ignore_case.description: Ignore ASCII case only: each letter matches its other case; no other character folds (a long s or a Kelvin sign reads as itself).

flag.description: The model id to suggest for this model and version. "{version}" is the seat's version.

yields.description: The exact model names this rule's templates spell, as the reader reads them back — a closed list, never a pattern, each name once. Absent or empty: the rule yields no model (a template that cannot fill, like an id a launch line shows but the screen never does).

version_like.description: The version shapes this rule can spell its models with: a regular expression source anchored at both ends ("^" and "$"), tested against the whole version. Absent: the rule spells no version. A source not anchored at both ends is refused as the profile loads.

absent.description: What a launch that names no model does. last-used: the CLI starts on whatever model it used last.

status_line.description: The status line's patterns: one string, or a list where one pattern per family would not fit the dialect's length cap. A line is a candidate when it matches any entry.

status_below.description: Where the status row must sit, declared only for a CLI whose captures show the pane drawing a workspace line under it. The line directly under the row must match `line` and be the pane's last non-blank one, and the `  →` input row must sit above the row within the distance the captures show; a grammar line anywhere else is ordinary text. A row matching `except` keeps its grammar-only reading, wherever it is — the reading it had before this field existed. A bare string is `line` with no exemption.

status.description: A box composer's status row, under its closing rule: the same shape `status_line` takes, read only for box-to-rule and only under the rule. Only a CLI whose capture shows a figure there declares it (grok's footer).

ignore_case.description: Ignore ASCII case only: each letter matches its other case; no other character folds (a long s or a Kelvin sign reads as itself). Only two-rules-footer-below reads it; a composer's other modes refuse the key at load.

wrap.description: How the composer continues a line onto its next row, declared only where a capture showed the wrap. The box is compared with the typed text under this rule: only the whitespace the row break itself stands for is normalised, the rest of every row must match character for character.

own_rows.description: Rows the pane draws of its own between the input row and the status row, declared only where a capture shows them. A matching row is not text in the box. Only status-then-one reads the key.

chrome.description: The pane's own chrome row under the status line: one string, or a list read as the union, each matching the whole line. Only status-then-one reads the key. Declared, a line under the status row is chrome only when it matches — any other line there leaves the row unread, so text the seat prints can never stand in for the pane's row and feed a quota figure. A composer that declares none keeps the trailing rule it had.

frame_rows.description: The empty rows a capture shows the pane drawing under the text, inside the box's frame (the drop before the status line or the closing rule). The box read strips up to this many trailing empty rows as the frame; a row beyond them is one the typed text does not have, and the box is refused. Zero where no capture shows such a row: don't guess.

border.description: The box's own border rows, declared only for a CLI whose captures draw them: `top` the row directly above the input row, `bottom` the row directly below the input rows and directly above the status row, both whole rows at one width (the captures draw them at the pane's width). The bordered frame is read beside the blank one; a frame with only one of the two rows, a row displaced from the input row or the status row, or a border-shaped row inside the box leaves the screen unknown. A composer without this field reads only the blank frame.
